chunks: Al-Fadl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Among the signs of the Relief is an event that will occur between the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina). I asked: And what is the event? He said: A tribal factionalism (asabiyyah) that will occur between the two Sanctuaries, and So-and-so from the descendants of So-and-so will kill fifteen 'leaders of the Arabs' (kabaash).

key_terms.الْفَرَج: The Relief (referring to the Reappearance of Imam Mahdi)
key_terms.بَيْنَ الْحَرَمَيْنِ: Between the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina)
key_terms.كَبْشًا: Ram (plural: kabaash, used metaphorically for leaders or chiefs)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the event between the two sanctuaries in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) identifies tribal factionalism (*asabiyya*) erupting between the two holy sanctuaries as a critical precursor to the Reappearance. The specific detail of fifteen leaders being killed, metaphorically termed 'rams' (*kabaash*), highlights the severity of the internal strife and the decisive action of a key figure from a specific lineage, underscoring the political and social turmoil preceding the Mahdi’s emergence.
